designs.title: YM4-04C: a localized polymer norm on the b = 2 blocked SU(2) action. One step, the self-map with a contraction, and the couplings where each one stops
designs.hypothesis_Hk: LATTICES AND MAP. Fine lattice Λ_0 = (Z/N)^4 with N = 2^K·L_K and L_K ≥ 4. The scale-k lattice Λ_k = (Z/(N/2^k))^4 has spacing 2^k a and comes from k applications of the YM4-03 line map at b = 2, (BU)_μ(x') = U_μ(2x')U_μ(2x'+e_μ). ρ_k is the exact Haar pushforward density (YM4-03 Theorem 4, iterated). GAUGE. At each step the line gauge (U_0,U_1) = (1,V_ℓ) is fixed at the coarse-link midpoint. It is a computational gauge only: every activity below is invariant under coarse gauge transformations, and every norm is a sup norm of an invariant function. H_0(β_0). ρ_0 is the SU(2) Wilson measure w = e^{β_0 a}, a = ½ Re Tr, written as ∏_p c_0(β_0)(1+K_p) with K = Σ_{n≥2} n t_n χ_{(n-1)/2}, t_n = I_n/I_1 and c_0(x) = Σ_m (x/2)^{2m}/(m!(m+1)!). H_k(κ, δ_k), k ≥ 1. log ρ_k(V) = const_k + Σ_Y R_k(Y;V). Y runs over finite sets of scale-k links with |Y| ≥ 4 that contain a closed loop. Each R_k(Y;·) is real, coarse-gauge invariant, and depends on V only through V|_Y. The localized polymer norm is ||R_k||_κ := sup_ℓ Σ_{Y∋ℓ} e^{κ|Y|} sup_V |R_k(Y;V)| ≤ δ_k. The coarse Wilson term (β_k/2)χ½(V_P) is carried inside R_k(∂P). PINNED CONSTANTS. κ = 1/4, the decay per link. D = 20, the maximum off-link adjacency degree of fine plaquettes. Six plaquettes per link, which gives Finner exponent 6. |W(e_0)| = 12, the off links of the 6 plaquettes through a line link. F_20(n) = C(20n,n)/(19n+1) and μ = 20^20/19^19. E|χ½| = 8/(3π) ≤ 8489/10000. n_max = 10. STEP-0 CERTIFICATE C_0(β_0). Let ε := ε_6(β_0) = ||K||_{L^6(SU(2))}. Let b range over {1/4 + i/64 : 0 ≤ i ≤ 128}, and let a be the least fixed point of a ↦ S(ε e^{2a+b}), computed by monotone iteration with upward rounding to 160 significant bits. Here S(x) := Σ_{n=4}^{10} N(n)x^n + Σ_{n≥11} 6F_20(n)x^n, with the series summed to n = 48 and the tail bounded by 6F_20(49)x^49/(1-μx). In the crude variant N(n) := 6F_20(n). In the refined variant N(n) := the maximum over off links e of the exact number of off-link-connected fine plaquette sets of n plaquettes that contain e and have every off link in at least 2 of their plaquettes (Lemma-B-closed). C_0 is MET iff some (a,b) has S ≤ a ≤ 1/4. Outputs: δ_1 := min 12a e^{-4(b-κ)}, and the readout c_½(P) ∈ 2t_2(β_0)^4 ± (8489/10000)·12a e^{-8b}. STEP-k CERTIFICATE C_k(δ_k), k ≥ 1. Set δ' := δ_k e^{δ_k}, a = t = δ' and b = κ. C_k is MET iff 2δ' ≤ κ/2. Output: δ_{k+1} ≤ c(δ_k)δ_k with c(δ) := e^{δ}[e^{-4κ} + max_{n≥4}(e^{-(κ/2-2δ')n} - e^{-κn/2})]. SELF-MAP. MET iff C_k holds and c(δ_k) < 1. Then δ_{k+j} ≤ c(δ_k)^j δ_k for every j, and Σ_k δ_k ≤ δ_k/(1-c). ADMISSIBLE. β_0 such that C_0 holds and δ_1 < δ_crit := sup{δ : C_k(δ) MET and c(δ) < 1}. UNIFORMITY. Every quantity is local: no bound involves N, K or the number of plaquettes. THEOREMS BEHIND THE CERTIFICATES. Both are to be DERIVED in the freeze note, before any engine code. G0: YM4-03C Lemmas A and B, plus Finner's inequality with exponent 6 (sup_V |z_γ| ≤ ε_6^{|γ|}), plus the Kotecký–Preiss criterion with a(γ) = a|off(γ)| ≤ 2a|γ|, d(γ) = b|γ|, and the test set W(e_0). This gives |Y''(γ)| ≤ |γ| and V-dependence only at size ≥ 4. G1: Y-objects in L^∞; Lemma A; the tree-graph bound Σ_{Γ∋e}∏ω ≤ t, which follows from Σ_{o∋e} ω_o e^{t s(o)} ≤ t; and the KP per-polymer corollary Σ_{𝒞∋Γ}|Φ|e^{d} ≤ |z_Γ|e^{a(Γ)+d(Γ)}. Together they give an exact line channel (factor e^{-κ|Y|/2} ≤ e^{-4κ}) plus a multi-object term.
designs.scope_and_non_claims: Strong bare coupling only, on finite periodic 4D tori whose last-scale sides are at least 4, at d = 4, b = 2 and κ = 1/4. What a MET means: an exact rational inequality chain (certificates C_0 and C_k) closes, or an exact enumeration or integral reads the predicted value. A MET means H_k ⇒ H_{k+1} only through theorems G0 and G1. The freeze note must derive both, and a second seat must attack them before the engine runs. The chain is tied to exact data by C09 (the YM4-03C series must lie inside the certified interval) and C10 (the exact line channel). The predicted windows are properties of this norm and these counts, with Fuss–Catalan growth of about 53 per plaquette against far smaller true surface counts: about β_0 ≤ 0.0196 for the self-map and ≤ 0.0208 for one step, below YM4-04B's Dobrushin reach of 1/18 and below 0.09 of one asymptotic-freedom step. A NOT_MET above the windows is a failure of the method. It is not evidence of a phase transition, a vanishing gap, or anything about the theory. Inside the window the certified flow goes to the trivial fixed point (Haar measure, β = 0), and C16 shows that the only UV-complete trajectory in the certified domain is the zero action. So nothing here constructs a renormalized trajectory with β(a) → ∞, relevant counterterms, a continuum limit, an infrared limit beyond fixed tori, OS reconstruction or a physical mass gap. Weak coupling, the crossover from β ≈ 0.02 to the scaling region, Balaban's small-field and large-field estimates, and YM4-04/05/06 all stay OPEN. No OPEN gate is promoted by these finite rows. Also not claimed: that the true contraction factor equals the certified one (e^{-4κ} is an attained lower bound on the hypothesis class and c(δ) an upper bound); that any exact count has been measured (C03 is a CONJECTURE until the engine runs); and anything for other κ, b or d. The predicted numbers come from design-lane scratch derivations in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b2fb539a-cb4d-5f0b-a22f-ca1a7fcb500d/scratchpad/ym4-04c/polymer-norm/ (derive_estimates.py, window2.py, delta_scan3.py, readout.py, contraction.py, induction_window.py, geometry_check.py). Those use Python Fractions and are not an engine. The engine must recompute every number in integers and rationals under the no-float gate.

rows.statement: Geometry and counting constants of the norm, on fine (Z/8)^4 and (Z/12)^4 with the b = 2 lines. Every link lies in 6 plaquettes. Every plaquette has 2 or 4 off links. The off-link adjacency graph of fine plaquettes has maximum degree D = 20 and minimum degree 10. For every line link e_0, the 6 plaquettes through it hold |W(e_0)| = 12 distinct off links. Every off link lies in 0 or 1 coarse filling. The Lemma-B-closed off-link-connected sets of at most 4 plaquettes are exactly the coarse fillings. The number of off-link-connected sets of n plaquettes containing a given off link is at most 6F_20(n), by a BFS injection into the complete 20-ary tree.
rows.predicted: 6 plaquettes per link; off links per plaquette in {2,4}; D = 20, minimum 10; |W| = 12 for every line link; on (Z/8)^4, 8192 off links in no filling and 6144 in exactly one; closed sets of at most 4 plaquettes are the fillings only, and none has 3 or fewer plaquettes. F_20(4..11) = 20540, 784245, 31763004, 1340246340, 58281448940, 2593593086150, 117544525178080, 5406686759963586. F_20(n+1)/F_20(n) is strictly increasing and below μ = 20^20/19^19 ∈ [53.00068, 53.00069] for n ≤ 59.
rows.method: Integer lattice enumeration with sites, links and plaquettes as coordinate tuples. A line link is one whose coordinates other than μ are all even. Exhaustive closed-set search up to 4 plaquettes, seeded at every off-link class. Fuss–Catalan numbers as exact binomials.
rows.falsifier: Any count different from the predicted one; a closed set of at most 4 plaquettes that is not a filling; an exact enumerated count in C03 above 6F_20(n); or a ratio F(n+1)/F(n) ≥ μ.
rows.reachable: 24,576 and 124,416 plaquettes. The census already ran on (Z/8)^4 in seconds in scratch (geometry_check.py: D = 20, minimum 10, |W| = 12, histogram 8192/6144). The Fuss–Catalan values are exact integers.

rows.statement: Per-plaquette activity in the Finner norm. ε_6(β) := ||e^{βa}/c_0(β) - 1||_{L^6(SU(2))}, with ε_6^6 = Σ_{k=0}^{6} C(6,k)(-1)^{6-k} c_0(kβ)/c_0(β)^k, read as rational enclosures. By Finner's inequality every fine polymer γ obeys sup_V |z_γ(V)| ≤ ε_6^{|γ|}, because an off link lies in at most 6 plaquettes.
rows.method: Exact rational partial sums of c_0 with geometric tail bounds; interval arithmetic through the alternating binomial sum; bisection for a rational sixth root to 10^-9.
rows.falsifier: An engine enclosure disjoint from a predicted one, or ε_6(β)/β outside [0.6538, 0.6551] at some β ≤ 1/10.
rows.reachable: Closed-form series. Scratch derive_estimates.py computed all nine enclosures with Fractions in under a minute.

rows.statement: Exact polymer counts. N(n) := the maximum over off links e of the number of Lemma-B-closed off-link-connected sets of n fine plaquettes containing e, for n = 4..10, read on fine (Z/8)^4 and (Z/12)^4.
rows.predicted: N(4) = 1 (the fillings; 0 on off links outside every filling). 12 ≤ N(6) ≤ 64 (the 12 unit cubes through any link give the lower bound). For 6 ≤ n ≤ 10, N(n) ≤ 10^-6·6F_20(n), that is N(6) ≤ 190, N(7) ≤ 8041, N(8) ≤ 349688, N(9) ≤ 15561558 and N(10) ≤ 705267151. The counts are identical on the two lattices.
rows.method: Exhaustive growth of plaquette sets containing a seed off link, connected through off links, with the open-link pruning of YM4-03C E2: an off link held once must be closed within the remaining size. Canonical forms under the coarse-compatible group (coarse translations × 384), one search per off-link class.
rows.falsifier: N(4) ≠ 1, N(6) < 12 or N(6) > 64, any N(n) above its predicted ceiling, or any count that differs between the two lattices.
rows.reachable: YM4-03C's search reached 166,079 states at 10 plaquettes for the V-dependent supports of one coarse link in 25–40 s. The vacuum-inclusive count adds closed surfaces anywhere along the set; the estimate is at most 10^8 states per off-link class at n = 10, a few hours on 4 cores in Rust. If the budget forces n_max = 8, that fallback is registered as new rows appended after the frozen ones, never as an edit.

rows.statement: The wall of the certificate. For b ≥ κ = 1/4 and every a > 0, x = ε_6 e^{2a+b} exceeds ε_6 e^{1/4}. Locate β_wall(κ=1/4) and, for comparison, the crossing μ ε_6 = 1 (κ → 0), on a 10^-5 grid.

rows.statement: The line channel sets the best uniform contraction on the hypothesis class. Take a scale-k input with no Wilson term and R_k(Y) = s·χ½ of each fine 2×2 loop on the next coarse plaquettes, where Y is the 8 line links of ∂P'', and every other R_k = 0. It blocks with no integral to R_{k+1}(∂P'') = s·χ½(V_{P''}), so δ_{k+1}/δ_k = e^{-4κ} exactly. At κ = 0 that ratio is 1, so the contraction is NOT_MET, and the pinned bound gives c(δ) ≥ e^{δ} > 1 at κ = 0.
rows.predicted: Ratio = e^{-1} ∈ [0.3678794, 0.3678795] at κ = 1/4, equal to the lower end of the c brackets in C07 and C08. Ratio = 1 at κ = 0: contraction NOT_MET. Certified c at κ = 0 ≥ 1: NOT_MET.
rows.method: Exact. The line-supported Y have no off links, so E_V factors out and log ρ_{k+1} gains R_k(Y) exactly (YM4-03 Proposition 2). The fine norm reads 12|s|e^{8κ}, from the 6 coarse plaquettes through each line link, and the coarse norm reads 12|s|e^{4κ}.
rows.falsifier: A ratio other than e^{-4κ}, a contraction read MET at κ = 0, or a certified c below e^{-4κ} at κ = 1/4, which this exact input would contradict.
rows.reachable: A few exact quaternion holonomies and two rational norm sums, in seconds.

designs.balaban_map: USED AND NAMED, NOT REPROVED. (1) Kotecký–Preiss, Commun. Math. Phys. 103 (1986) 491–498: the polymer convergence criterion, its test-set form, and the per-polymer corollary Σ_{𝒞∋γ}|Φ|e^{d} ≤ |z_γ|e^{a(γ)+d(γ)}. (2) Finner's generalized Hölder inequality, Ann. Probab. 20 (1992) 1893–1901, with exponent 6 because a link lies in 6 plaquettes. (3) Fuss–Catalan counts of subtrees of the complete D-ary tree (e.g. Graham–Knuth–Patashnik §7.5), with the BFS injection derived in the note. (4) The character expansion of the Wilson weight with Bessel ratios t_n = I_n/I_1 and the series c_0 = 2I_1/β. (5) The high-temperature polymer expansion of lattice gauge theory in the tradition of Osterwalder–Seiler (1978), NAMED with its body CANNOT_SEE in this repo, applied here to the line-conditioned measure. (6) Repo results: YM4-03 Theorem 4 and Proposition 2, and YM4-03C Lemmas A, B and C (DERIVED, merged); the YM4-03C receipt coefficients (MEASURED) serve as the control series. (7) A tree-graph (Penrose-type) bound for collections of objects, derived in the note. TESTED, AS A STRONG-COUPLING ANALOG ONLY. The shape of Balaban's effective-density bound, as GPT-6 read CMP 122 Theorem 1: χ_k exp(-g_k^{-2}A - E_-|T|) ≤ ρ_k ≤ exp(E_+|T|), with E_± independent of k and volume. H_k gives |log ρ_k - const| ≤ (#links/(4e))δ_k, with δ_k independent of L and decreasing geometrically in k. But this sits at g_k^{-2} → 0 (strong coupling), not g_k → 0. The norm template e^{κ|X|} is Brydges' localized polymer norm; here it carries only sup norms, with no field derivatives or analyticity domains. NOT REACHED, STILL UNPROVED. Balaban's small-field/large-field decomposition and its large-field suppression; averaging block-spin maps with gauge fixing inside blocks (Dimock's expositions, arXiv:1108.1335 and 1712.10029, credit the method to Balaban); Gaussian background-field integration and the effective-coupling flow g_{k+1}(g_k); Balaban's Theorem 2, which removes the assumption on the effective couplings and is unpublished per GPT-6's reading; uniqueness of the UV limit. Also unproved: any rigorous control of the crossover from β_0 ≈ 0.02 to the scaling region, since no known method covers it, and the one-loop running Δβ ≈ 0.2575 per halving, of which the certified window is under 9%. Relevant counterterms are not tested: in the certified flow the plaquette coupling is irrelevant-like (about β^4/64). Possible non-quasilocality of the line decimation at weak coupling (the analog of van Enter–Fernández–Sokal for spin systems) would rule out any κ-norm there. It is a CONJECTURE that this experiment cannot decide. Mass gap (YM4-06) and OS reconstruction (YM4-05): OPEN.
risks: G0 and G1 are only sketched in this design. If the KP per-polymer corollary, the test-set step or the root-object bookkeeping in G1 (the formula for c(δ)) is wrong, then C07, C08, C11–C14 and C16 read the arithmetic of an invalid bound. Mitigations: C09 (the YM4-03C series must lie inside the certified interval), C10 (the exact line channel bounds c from below), and a second-seat attack on the freeze note before any engine code.

The windows are set by counting: Fuss–Catalan growth μ ≈ 53 per plaquette against far smaller true surface counts. A reader may take NOT_MET above β ≈ 0.02 as physics. The rows and the scope say it is a method limit.

The localized polymer window (about 0.02) reaches less far in β than YM4-04B's Dobrushin correlation bound (1/18). The new content is control of the effective action itself, uniform in volume and summable over k, not a weaker coupling. Overselling it as weak-coupling progress would be wrong.

The exact enumeration to n = 10, vacuum surfaces included, may exceed the compute budget (estimated up to 10^8 states per off-link class). A fallback to n_max = 8 would change C03, C06, C08, C09 and C14, and must be filed as appended rows, never as edits to frozen ones.

The predicted edges are read on pinned grids: b in steps of 1/64, β in steps of 10^-5, a as a least fixed point with 160-bit upward rounding. A different grid moves an edge by less than 10^-4, and the brackets carry that tolerance. An engine that silently uses another grid could miss a row for that reason alone.
κ = 1/4 is the only decay rate tested. The tradeoff (larger κ contracts faster but narrows the window through b ≥ κ) is unmeasured, and so is any optimum.
For k ≥ 1 the coarse Wilson term is carried inside R_k as a Y-object, which forfeits Lemma B. That is harmless at these tiny δ, but any extension toward larger coarse couplings must restore it.

Finite tori only, with last-scale sides ≥ 4. Wrapping polymers beyond n_max are covered by the degree-20 Fuss–Catalan bound on any graph, but the exact counts assume nothing wraps within 10 plaquettes at fine side ≥ 8.

The scratch derivations behind the predicted numbers are Python Fractions in the design lane's scratchpad. Two display lines converted to float for printing or for a scan range. The engine must recompute everything in integers and rationals under the repo's no-float gate.
The one-loop asymptotic-freedom comparison (Δβ = (11/(3π²)) ln 2 per halving) gives scale only; the experiment does not and cannot test asymptotic freedom.

designs.title: YM4-04C: the small-field/large-field split across one b = 2 line-map step. Exact SU(2) one-link atoms, the exact Gaussian step and chessboard large-field bounds, at β = 16 to 4096
designs.hypothesis_Hk:
H_k sets G = SU(2), d = 4, b = 2, with the YM4-03 line map B, at scale k >= 0.

DATA. The lattice is the periodic Λ_k = (Z/L_k)^4 with L_k = 2^-k L_0 and spacing a_k = 2^k a_0. The measure is ν_k = (B^k)_* μ_{β_0}, with density ρ_k against product Haar (exact by YM4-03 Thm 4). The fine measure is the Wilson measure exp(-β Σ_p (1 - a(U_p))), with a(g) = Re Tr g / 2.

NORM ON THE GROUP. |1 - g| is the Euclidean distance on S^3 in R^4, so 1 - a(g) = |1 - g|^2 / 2, which lies in [0, 2]. Compactness means any threshold >= 2 is vacuous.

ADMISSIBLE COUPLINGS AND SCALES. β_k is in [16, ∞), and the experiment uses the grid {16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096}. The threshold parameter satisfies p_k^2 >= 1, and ε_k = 2 p_k^2 / β_k. Equivalently, |1 - V_p| <= p_k g_k with g_k^2 = 4/β_k. The trajectory β_{k+1} = β_k - b0' + O(1/β_k), with b0' = 11 log 2/(3π^2) in [0.2575118068, 0.2575118069], is never assumed by any row.

SMALL-FIELD REGION. Ω_k = {V : 1 - a(V_p) <= ε_k for every plaquette p of Λ_k}. It is gauge invariant. Its complement is the union over p of {1 - a(V_p) > ε_k}, with large-field set P_L(V) = {p : 1 - a(V_p) > ε_k}.

(LF_k) LARGE-FIELD SUPPRESSION, polymer form. For every set X of distinct plaquettes of Λ_k:
  ν_k(1 - a(V_p) > ε_k for all p in X) <= exp(-c_LF p_k^2 |X|).

(SF_k) NEAR-GAUSSIAN SMALL-FIELD BOUND. For V in Ω_k:
  -log ρ_k(V) = c_k + β_k Q_k(V) + R_k(V).
- Q_k is a β-independent, gauge-invariant quadratic form in the linearized curvature. Q_0 = Σ_p (1 - a(V_p)), the Wilson form. For k >= 1, Q_k is the k-fold Gaussian line-map blocked form, normalized to transverse coefficient 1 at zero momentum, with kernel decay rate κ_Q > 0.
- R_k = Σ_X R_{k,X}, summed over connected X in Λ_k. Each R_{k,X} depends on V|_X and is gauge invariant.
- Norm: ||R_k||_{κ,k} = sup_x Σ_{X ∋ x} e^{κ|X|} sup_{V in Ω_k} |R_{k,X}(V)| <= η_k. The non-marginal part, after its marginal part is moved into β_{k+1}, satisfies η_k <= C_R p_k^4 / β_k, and η_{k+1} <= θ η_k + C β_k^-2 with θ < 1.

CONSTANTS. c_LF, C_R, κ, κ_Q > 0 and θ < 1 are independent of k, of L_0 (the ultraviolet cutoff) and of the volume.

GAUGES. No invariant statement fixes a gauge. Gauges appear only inside computations of invariant numbers:
- a maximal tree in the lower bound on Z (R03), exact for gauge-invariant integrands;
- the Feynman gauge in Gaussian covariances (R09 to R12), read only on gauge-invariant transverse modes and loop fluxes;
- the line gauge (U_0, U_1) = (1, V) of YM4-03C for pushforward identities.

STATUS. H_0 holds with Q_0 Wilson and R_0 = 0, and its LF_0 is what R03 bounds. The step H_k => H_{k+1} is NOT tested. The rows test its ingredients at k = 0 -> 1 and test the choice of the line map.

rows.statement:
Gauge separation on fine (Z/4)^4 and coarse (Z/2)^4.

Setup:
- 4 seeded exact rational SU(2) configurations. Each link is a unit quaternion from the Cayley map w -> ((1-|w|^2) + 2w)/(1+|w|^2), with w in Q^3.
- 4 seeded rational gauge transformations per configuration.

(a) The following are unchanged by every gauge transformation (YM4-01; YM4-03 Thm 1):
- every fine plaquette value a(U_p);
- every coarse plaquette value a((BU)_p');
- hence membership of U in Ω_0 and of BU in Ω_1, at ε in {1/64, 1/256}.

(b) The gauge-variant link condition max_l (1 - a(U_l)) <= ε is NOT invariant. The gauge transform of U ≡ 1 has every plaquette equal to 1, so it lies in Ω_0 at every ε, yet it fails the link condition.

Every later invariant statement uses Ω_k only.
rows.predicted:
(a) MET on all 16 pairs, at both levels and both ε. 0 changed values among the 16 × (1536 + 96) plaquette words.
(b) The link condition flips membership on 4 of 4 seeds.
rows.method: Exact quaternion products over Q, with a(g) read as the real part. Values are compared as rationals before and after U_l -> g(x) U_l g(x+l)^-1.
rows.falsifier: Any fine or coarse plaquette value that changes under a gauge transformation. Or the link-based condition keeping its membership unchanged on all 4 seeds.
rows.reachable: 1632 plaquette words × 16 pairs × 2 thresholds of rational quaternion products. Seconds in Python.

rows.statement:
Take a fine 2×2 tile with plaquettes p_1..p_4 and boundary holonomy V', the coarse plaquette (YM4-03 Prop 2).

Bound: |1 - V'| <= Σ_i |1 - U_{p_i}|. This follows from the lasso decomposition, |1 - gh| <= |1 - g| + |1 - h|, and conjugation invariance. Hence
  1 - a(V') <= 4 Σ_i (1 - a(U_{p_i})) <= 16 max_i (1 - a(U_{p_i})).

Sharpness: the constant 16 = b^4 is attained. Take the abelian constant-field tile U_1 = 1, U_2(x) = q^{x_1}, with q = cos θ + k sin θ rational. Every fine plaquette has 1 - a = ε, and 1 - a(V') = 1 - T_4(1 - ε). The ratio is 16 - 40ε + 32ε^2 - 8ε^3.

Consequence (an error-growing recurrence surfaced): deterministic propagation of the small-field set needs ε_{k+1} >= 16 ε_k (1 - O(ε_k)), that is p_{k+1}^2 >= 16 p_k^2 β_{k+1}/β_k. So Ω_{k+1} must be defined on the coarse field and paid for by LF_{k+1}.
rows.method: Exact rational quaternion arithmetic on the tile's 12 links. 1 - a(V') is compared as a rational with 4 Σ (1 - a_i) and with 16 max_i (1 - a_i). The aligned ratios are compared with the stated rationals.
rows.falsifier: A tile violating either inequality. Or an aligned ratio different from its stated rational.
rows.reachable: 10^4 tiles of 16 quaternion products each. Seconds.

rows.statement:
Large-field suppression for the full fine SU(2) Wilson measure on (Z/L)^4, L in {4, 8}.

Bound: for every plaquette p and every ε in (0, 2],
  μ_β(1 - a(U_p) > ε) <= exp(-βε + Φ_0(β, L)),
with Φ_0 = (1/N_s)[-N_f log h(t*) + (3/2) N_f].

Definitions:
- N_f = 3 N_s + 1, the number of non-tree links.
- t* = 3 N_f / (32 β N_p).
- h(t) = (2θ - sin 2θ)/(2π), with cos θ = 1 - t (the Haar measure of the cap).

Ingredients:
1. The chessboard estimate over the N_s plaquettes of one orientation. This is NAMED (FILS 1978, Thm 4.1), applied with site reflection positivity in-plane and link reflection positivity (β >= 0) transverse, both from Lemma 0004.
2. The exact maximal-tree identity for Z.
3. Restriction of the non-tree links to the cap 1 - a <= t*.
4. |1 - U_p| <= Σ_{l in p} |1 - U_l|, so 1 - a(U_p) <= 16 t*.
rows.method:
Rational interval arithmetic with outward dyadic rounding:
- arcsin, sqrt and atanh-log series;
- π by Machin.
Enclosure width <= 1e-9. The chessboard step is NAMED, and its recipe is tested in two dimensions by R05.
rows.reachable: Ten closed-form evaluations, under 1 s. The prediction lane's check ran in 0.15 s.

rows.statement:
The large-field bound one blocking step inherits from the fine action alone, for the coarse plaquette V' (a fine 2×2 loop). Lattices: coarse 2^4 and 4^4.

Union route, via R02:
  ν(1 - a(V') > ε') <= 4 exp(-βε'/16 + Φ_0).
This is nontrivial iff ε' > ε'_∪ = 16 (Φ_0 + log 4)/β.

Coarse-chessboard route. ν is reflection positive by YM4-03 Thm 6. Cauchy–Schwarz over the 4 plaquettes of each filling gives Σ_filling (1 - a) >= (1 - a(V'))/4, and the fillings are plaquette-disjoint. Then
  ν(1 - a(V') > ε') <= exp(-βε'/4 + 16 Φ_0),
which is nontrivial iff ε' > ε'_□ = 64 Φ_0/β.

Consequence: the inherited threshold grows by at least b^d = 16 per step, so after k steps it is at least 16^k ε*. It becomes vacuous once 16^k > 2β/Φ_0. LF_{k+1} must therefore come from ρ_{k+1}'s own effective action, which is OPEN.
rows.method: Exact rational arithmetic on the R03 enclosures. The Cauchy–Schwarz and union inequalities are checked on R02's 10^4 tiles and its aligned tiles.
rows.reachable: Arithmetic on R03's output plus R02's tiles. Seconds.

rows.statement:
A check of the chessboard recipe where the truth is exact: continuous SU(2) Wilson on the two-dimensional torus (Z/4)^2, with N_s = N_p = 16.

The exact single-plaquette law is
  f(g) = w_β(g) Σ_n c_n^15 χ_n(g)/n / Σ_n c_n^16,  with c_n = (2/β) I_n(β)
(genus-1 gluing). From it, P_T(β, c) = P(1 - a(U_p) > c/β).

Points: β in {16, 64, 256}, c in {8, 16}.

The chessboard bound with the exact Z is
  Bnd = e^-c (e^{-16β} Σ_n c_n^16)^{-1/16}.
rows.predicted:
MET: P_T <= Bnd at all 6 points, with Bnd/P_T >= 10.

The entropy-free bound e^-c is FALSE (NOT_MET) at β in {64, 256}, for both c: there P_T > 1.2 e^-c. So the entropy term is necessary.

The bound with the orbit inflated 256× (exponent 1/4096) is also NOT_MET at β in {64, 256}.
rows.method:
Exact character sums.
- t_n = I_n/I_1 are exact positive rational series, with certified tails by Amos' bound.
- ∫ w χ_n 1_large by Clebsch–Gordan, χ_m χ_n = Σ χ_k.
- ∫ χ_k 1_large is in closed form: (1/π)[sin((k+1)θ_ε)/(k+1) - sin((k-1)θ_ε)/(k-1)], with the k = 1 term involving π - θ_ε.
- θ_ε, π, sqrt and exp are enclosed rationally.
rows.reachable: n, m up to about 200 at β = 256, so triple sums of about 10^7 rational operations with dyadic rounding. Minutes.

rows.statement:
Exact one-link decimation in a frozen four-dimensional environment.

One fine link U is integrated against its six plaquettes. The staples A_1..A_6 (unit quaternions v_i, in three planes) are fixed. Then
  Z_β(Q) = ∫ exp(β Σ_i a(U A_i)) dU = Σ_m (β^2 Q/4)^m / (m!(m+1)!),
with Q = 36 - 2D and D = Σ_{i<j} (1 - a(A_i^-1 A_j)).

The sum D runs over the 15 six-link loops: 3 planar 1×2 rectangles and 12 chairs (YM4-05A). The induced action is S_ind = -log Z.

Its linear (Wilson) coefficient on each of the 15 loops is
  β_loop(β) = dS_ind/dD at D = 0 = (β/6) I_2(6β)/I_1(6β).

So decimation spreads 6 plaquettes at β onto 15 loops at β/6, with an exact fluctuation shift of -1/24 per loop.
rows.method:
I_2/I_1 at x = 6β is the ratio of two positive rational series:
  (3β) Σ (9β^2)^m/(m!(m+2)!) / Σ (9β^2)^m/(m!(m+1)!).
Partial sums are exact, with certified geometric tails once the term ratio is below 1/2, and outward dyadic rounding.
rows.falsifier: An exact enclosure of β_loop - (β/6 - 1/24) outside the stated bracket at any β.
rows.reachable: About 3β + 30√β terms, so 16,000 at β = 4096. Seconds to one minute.

rows.statement:
The remainder R_β(D) = S_ind(36 - 2D) - S_ind(36) - β_loop D.

(a) [DERIVED] R_β is convex on [0, 18], with R(0) = R'(0) = 0, so R >= 0 and R is nondecreasing.
Certificate: -(log Z)_QQ = (β^4/(4x^2)) (r^2 + 4r/x - 1), with r = I_2/I_1 and x = β√Q. Amos' lower bound r >= x/(2 + √(4 + x^2)) (NAMED) makes r^2 + 4r/x - 1 >= 0.

(b) [leading term DERIVED from the expansion of √Q: R ≈ β D^2/432] The atom's post-step small-field region is SF(ε) = {all 15 loops have 1 - a <= ε}. On it D <= 15ε, so the supremum of R over SF(2p^2/β) is at most R(30p^2/β). Predicted:
  R(30p^2/β) = (25p^4/(12β)) (1 + (5p^2/6 - 1/2)/β + δ).
This is a near-Gaussian bound O(g^2 p^4).

(c) [DERIVED] R holds products of distinct loops (chair×chair, chair×rectangle) with coefficient φ''(0) = β/216 - 1/432 + O(1/β). So the induced action is not a sum of single loops.
rows.method: Clauses (a) and (c) are DERIVED. Exact series for Z at rational Q = 36 - 2D: no square root appears, since Z depends on β^2 Q. The certificate compares the r it uses with the exact r enclosure. φ'' is read from the exact series of Z, Z' and Z''.
rows.reachable: 8 (β, p) points × 3 series evaluations, each up to about 16,000 terms. Minutes.

rows.statement:
Large-field suppression in the atom, with aligned staples: A_i = A for all i, so Q = 36 is maximal.

The conditional law of s = 6β(1 - a(UA)) has density proportional to e^-s √s √(1 - s/(12β)) on [0, 12β]. At ε = 2p^2/β,
  P_atom(β, ε) = P(s > 12p^2).

[DERIVED, by monotone likelihood ratio in κ = 6β] P_atom is strictly increasing in β. P_atom < Q(3/2, 12p^2) = P(χ^2_3 > 24p^2) for every β, with that value as its limit.

Consequence: at fixed p the per-plaquette large-field probability tends to a positive constant. It does not decay with β, so suppression needs p_k -> ∞, which is Balaban's p(g) mechanism. Here P_atom is far below e^{-βε} = e^{-2p^2}, while in two dimensions (R05) the single plaquette sits above e^{-βε}.
rows.reachable: β <= 1024 (κ <= 6144), n up to about 1000. Minutes.

rows.statement:
The Gaussian reference measure: the β -> ∞ linearization, three abelian copies with action (β/8) Σ_p |F_p|^2, with gauge and harmonic modes removed, on (Z/L)^4.

Claim: β <1 - a(U_p)>_G = (3/2) V_11, where V_11 = 4 (G_L(0) - G_L(e_1)) = (1/2)(1 - 1/N_s), and G_L is the torus Green's function.

This is the control for the Green's-function engine that R12 uses.
rows.method: Exact orbit-reduced Poisson solve ΔG_L = δ - 1/N_s with Σ G_L = 0, under the hyperoctahedral symmetry. Orbit counts: 15 (L = 4), 70 (L = 8), 495 (L = 16) rational unknowns.
rows.falsifier: Any other value.
rows.reachable: A 495×495 sparse exact rational solve. Minutes in Python, seconds in Rust.

rows.statement:
The exact Gaussian b = 2 line-map step, transverse sector.

Take coarse Bloch momentum k' = κ e_1 and polarization e_2. Let ρ_d(S) be the coarse precision divided by its Wilson value (β/4)·4S, where S = sin^2(κ/2).

Aliasing gives (1/2^d) Σ_{l in {0,1}^d} |B_2(q_l)|^2/q̂_l^2, with q_l = (k' + 2πl)/2. Then:
- d = 4: ρ_4(S) = 4/(4 + 24S/(S+8) + 20S/(S+24));
- d = 3: ρ_3(S) = 2/(4 + 12S/(S+8));
- d = 2: ρ_2 = 1/4, constant.

So β'_G = lim ρ = 2^{d-4} β. In d = 4 that is β: the Gaussian step is marginal and carries no coupling flow, so asymptotic freedom lies beyond it. In d = 2 it is β/4, YM4-03 Thm 8 linearized.

ρ_4 < 1 and strictly decreasing in S, so the blocked Gaussian form is not Wilson-quadratic at any nonzero momentum.
rows.method: Engine: the exact Schur complement, meaning minimization over the fiber ker B of the fine Bloch cell problem. The cell has 64 links in d = 4, 16 in d = 2, and 32 in d = 3. The Bloch phase is e^{iκ} = ((1 - t^2) + 2it)/(1 + t^2), over Q(i). The transverse eigenvalue of the coarse form is then read. Independent check: the aliasing sum above, in separate code.
rows.falsifier: Any computed ρ different from its stated rational.
rows.reachable: About 18 Bloch sectors of 64×64 Hermitian matrices over Q(i). Seconds.

rows.statement:
The Gaussian fluctuation operator of one line-map step: d^T d (the Hessian of (1/2) Σ F^2, per color; multiply by β/4 for SU(2)) restricted to the fiber intersected with the orthogonal complement of the fiber gauge directions. That space has 45 dimensions per coarse cell.

(a) [DERIVED] It is positive definite in every Bloch sector: a closed fiber vector is a fiber gauge direction. Hence it is uniformly positive over the coarse Brillouin zone, by continuity and compactness.

(b) [DERIVED] In the k' = 0 sector its lowest eigenvalue λ_0* is the smallest root of λ^3 - 18λ^2 + 80λ - 48, with multiplicity 4. This comes from the secular equation λ Σ_q 1/(λ_q - λ) = 1 over the B-coupled transverse modes {4, 4, 4, 8, 8, 8, 12} of the 2^4 cell.

(c) [CONJECTURE] The minimum over all computed sectors lies in [0.35, λ_0*]. The computed sectors are:
- the 16 sectors of fine 4^4;
- the 256 sectors of fine 8^4;
- twisted sectors with t in {1/2, 1/4, 1/8} along an axis and along the diagonal.
Also min_{8^4} >= min_{4^4}/2.

Note: a computed minimum is only an upper bound on the infinite-volume gap. A lower bound over the whole zone needs a covering certificate, which is OPEN.
rows.predicted:
(a) No eigenvalue <= 0 in any sector.
(b) λ_0* in [0.7084973778, 0.7084973779], multiplicity 4 (cross-read in the prediction lane by exact inertia: 0 eigenvalues below 7/10, 4 below 71/100).
(c) Minimum in [0.35, 0.7084973779].
rows.method: Clauses (a) and (b) are DERIVED. Build an exact rational or Q(i) basis of the physical fiber per sector. Count eigenvalues below λ by exact LDL^T inertia of K - λG. Bisect to 1e-9, shifting off exact rational eigenvalues to avoid zero pivots.
rows.falsifier: A nonpositive eigenvalue in any sector. Or a k' = 0 value outside the bracket or with another multiplicity. Or a computed minimum below 0.35.
rows.reachable: About 30 symmetry classes of sectors × 40 LDLs of 45×45 matrices. Minutes.

rows.statement:
The line-map coarse field gets rougher with scale. Define the Gaussian variance ratio
  r_k = V(2^k × 2^k)/V(1×1),
where V(C) = Σ_{l,l' in C} s_l s_l' G_L(x_l - x_l'). This is the flux variance of the scale-k coarse plaquette, a fine 2^k × 2^k Wilson loop; it is gauge invariant and computed in Feynman gauge.

[DERIVED] In infinite volume, r_{k+1}/r_k -> 2, by the perimeter law.

Consequence: at fixed p, the Gaussian large-field probability of the scale-k coarse plaquette is Q(3/2, 4p^2/r_k), which grows with k. So no line-map H_k with fixed or slowly growing p holds, even at the Gaussian level. That would need ε_k ~ 2^k/β_k, which ends after O(log β) steps. Verdict: YM4-04 needs a block average, as YM4-03 §7 conjectured.
rows.method: Exact torus Green's function from R09's orbit-reduced solve, then exact rational sums over loop link pairs. Q(3/2, y) by rational series.
rows.falsifier: Any r outside its interval. Or r_2/r_1 below 2.2 on 16^4.
rows.reachable: G_L at about 50 separations from 70 or 495 unknowns. Minutes.

rows.statement:
Two-dimensional exact full step: a disk, b = 2, continuous SU(2). The fine plaquettes are i.i.d. with law w_β, and the coarse plaquette has law w_β^{*4} (YM4-03 Thm 8).

Points: ε = c/β with c in {2, 8}, and β in {64, 256, 1024}.

(a) [DERIVED] P_fine(c/β) is strictly increasing in β, below Q(3/2, c), with that value as its limit.
(b) [DERIVED] P_coarse(4c/β) has the same limit: as β -> ∞ the large-field probability is scale-covariant at threshold × b^2, because β' = β/4.
(c) [DERIVED] P_coarse(16c/β) <= 4 P_fine(c/β), by the union bound via R02.
(d) [CONJECTURE] Both:
- |P_coarse(4c/β)/P_fine(c/β) - 1| <= (c^2 + 4c)/β;
- (1 - P_fine/Q)β in [0.5, 1.5] × κ_1(c).

Contrast with d = 4: there β' = β (R10), the line-map threshold for equal probability grows by about r_1 (R12), and it grows by 16 in the worst case (R02).

rows.statement:
Surfacing a divergent recurrence.

Along β_{k+1} = β_k - b0', with b0' = 11 log 2/(3π^2), from β_0 down to the last β_k >= 16:
  Σ_k 1/β_k >= (1/b0') log(β_0/16),
which is unbounded as β_0 -> ∞, that is as a -> 0. Meanwhile Σ_k 1/β_k^2 <= 1/256 + 1/(16 b0') uniformly.

So a remainder bound of the atom's form, η_k = (25/12) p^4/β_k (R07), summed without contraction, diverges with the ultraviolet cutoff. H_k => H_{k+1} must move the marginal O(1/β_k) part into β_{k+1}, and carry a contraction θ < 1 or an O(β_k^-2) bound on the rest.
rows.method: Rational enclosures of log 2 and π. Integral comparisons of the monotone sums, plus exact partial sums of the first 10^4 terms as a cross-check.
rows.falsifier: A certified lower bound below the stated value, or an upper bound on Σ 1/β_k^2 above 0.2467.
rows.reachable: Instant.

risks: The chessboard estimate's use for plaquette indicators is NAMED, not proved here. It mixes site reflections in-plane with link reflections transverse, and the orbit size N_s is the crux. R05 checks the recipe only in two dimensions, against exact truth.
The Gaussian rows (R09 to R12) describe the β → ∞ linearization. Carrying them to SU(2) at finite β needs the OPEN SF bound. R12's verdict on the line map holds at the Gaussian level only.

R12's intervals rest on asymptotic estimates of the lattice Green's function. R11(c)'s lower bound 0.35 is a guess, and R07's and R08's brackets are asymptotic. Any of these CONJECTURE rows may miss, and a miss is to be filed.
The atom freezes its environment. It is a one-link decimation, not the b = 2 step, and it says nothing about how staples are distributed under ν_k.

Several DERIVED rows (R03, R04, R14) are arithmetic of closed forms that the prediction lane already evaluated in scratch scripts. Their falsifiers test the engine's independent arithmetic and the inequalities (R02, R05), and add no new physics. The k' = 0 clause of R11 was cross-read by exact inertia before the freeze. All of this must be disclosed.
Exact Bessel series at β = 4096 and Clebsch–Gordan triple sums need outward dyadic rounding to keep integer sizes bounded. Uncertified truncation would void the enclosures.
The Bloch computations over Q(i) meet exact rational eigenvalues, for example 4 in the k' = 0 sector, which give zero LDL pivots. Bisection must shift off them.
Line-map specificity: a MET reading of R12 refutes only a line-map H_k, and a positive R11 does not establish SF_1. An averaging map would need its own prediction set.

designs.title: YM4-04C coupling trajectory: one-step SU(2) effective couplings, exact at strong coupling and at tree level, certified where reachable, with the line map's thin-line failure
designs.hypothesis_Hk: H_k(M), the coupling part of a YM4-04 induction, as far as this step can test it. SCALES: fine spacing a on the fine torus (Z/2^k L)^4; coarse torus Lambda_k = (Z/L)^4 at spacing 2^k a, with L >= 3, or L = 4 where p = pi is needed. M_k = M o ... o M (k times). Two maps: M = B, the YM4-03 line map at b = 2, which composes exactly (B o B = B_4); and M = A, the block average of 2-step parallel transporters over the 2^4 offsets of a block. A is defined here only through its abelian linearization, which also composes exactly (A o A = A_4). MEASURE: rho_k = (M_k)_* mu_beta, continuous SU(2) Wilson, beta = 4/g^2. COUPLING (gauge invariant, no gauge fixing): beta_k(p) := 4 H_{log rho_k}(X_p) / sum_P phi_P(X_p)^2, where H_f(X) = -d^2/de^2 f(exp(eX)) at e = 0 and X_p is the abelian sigma_3 coarse plane wave x_mu(x') = cos(p.x') with polarization mu perpendicular to p. This is normalized so that a coarse Wilson action at beta' reads beta_k = beta'. Define beta_k := lim_{p->0} beta_k(kappa e_nu). NORM of the irrelevant part: N_k := sup_{p != 0} |beta_k/beta_k(p) - 1| / phat^2. At tree level its p -> 0 value is the slope A_k, defined by r_k(p) = 1/(1 + A_k phat^2 + O(phat^4)), and its corner value is (1/r_k(pi) - 1)/4. H_k ASSERTS, with gamma and C independent of k and L: (i) STRONG COUPLING, beta <= beta_cert: beta_{k+1} = 4(beta_k/4)^4 (1 - beta_k^2/6 + O(beta_k^4)), with the exact series through beta^10 and a certified remainder. (ii) TREE LEVEL (beta -> infinity): beta_{k+1}/beta_k -> 1 (classical marginality in d = 4) and N_k^tree <= C. (iii) WEAK COUPLING, g_k^2 <= gamma: beta_{k+1} = beta_k - c0 - c1/beta_k + delta_k with |delta_k| <= C/beta_k^2 and the sum over k of |delta_k| finite along the trajectory, where c0 = 11 ln2/(3 pi^2) and c1 = 17 ln2/(3 pi^4) (SU(2), b = 2; b0 = 11/(24 pi^2), b1 = 17/(96 pi^4)). (iv) SCHEME: the other gauge-invariant readouts differ from beta_k by a bounded, k-uniform amount. These are beta^S (twice the chi_1/2(V_P) projection of log rho_k in coarse Haar) and beta^chi (matching <chi_1/2(V_P)> against coarse Wilson). WHAT THE STEP TESTS: (i) through beta^10 (beta^12 for one split), certified only for beta <= 2^-22 by the YM4-04A global Cauchy bound. (ii) exactly for k = 1, 2, 3, predicting that it FAILS for M = B (A_k grows like G_3(0) 2^k, the corner coupling halves per step) and HOLDS for M = A (A_k -> -1/6 geometrically). (iv) at strong coupling and exactly in d = 2. (iii)'s constants are frozen as targets and not tested. The implication H_k => H_{k+1} is tested nowhere in this step.
designs.scope_and_non_claims: SCOPE: finite periodic lattices. In 4D: fine 6^4 -> coarse 3^4 for strong coupling, fine 8^4 -> coarse 4^4 for p = pi and beta^12, and fine (Z/2b)^4 -> coarse 2^4 for tree level at b = 2, 4, 8. The maps are the YM4-03 b = 2 line map with its exact compositions B_4 and B_8, and the abelian linearization of a block-averaged map as a comparator. Controls in d = 2 (exact at every beta by Theorem 8) and d = 3. REACHABLE AND READ: (1) 4D strong coupling: exact formal series of three gauge-invariant one-step couplings (beta'_q, beta'_S, beta'_chi) through beta^10, one split at beta^12, and a certified enclosure only for beta <= 2^-22. (2) 4D weak coupling: tree level only, i.e. lim beta_k/beta, exactly, for k = 1, 2, 3. (3) d = 2: exact at all beta, from strong coupling to beta = 4096, including the exact multi-step trajectory. THE HONEST BOUNDARY: no row reads a 4D coupling at any beta between 2^-21 and the tree-level limit. The one-loop and two-loop running in 4D (c0, c1) is frozen as a target and never computed. A one-step shift from the Wilson action is scheme dependent, so even an exact one-loop computation of a single step would not isolate c0. NOT CLAIMED: H_k => H_{k+1}; any certified 4D coupling at beta > 2^-22; asymptotic freedom; uniformity in volume beyond the local strong-coupling coefficients; large-field control; a non-abelian averaged map with positivity or reflection positivity; first-state visibility; a mass gap; the continuum; the Clay problem. A MET on a tree-level row is not evidence of asymptotic freedom. The predicted NOT_MET of the line map's uniform tree-level norm concerns that map at tree level only. No floats in any proposed engine. The design-lane derivation checks are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/b2fb539a-cb4d-5f0b-a22f-ca1a7fcb500d/scratchpad/ym4-04c/coupling-trajectory/ (d1_strong.py, d2_toy_split.py, d3_tree.py, d5_tree_exact.py, d6_two_d.py, d7_hessian_chairs.py, d8_misc.py, d9_window.py). They are Fractions-only except d3/d6, which use Decimal, and d4, which is a numpy float sanity run. They fixed the frozen numbers and are not evidence. The repo was read only, at main 830fd3f.

rows.statement: Small-field one-step coupling at strong coupling, axis momenta. On fine 6^4 -> coarse 3^4 (d = 4) and fine 6^3 -> coarse 3^3 (d = 3), beta'_q(beta; p) := 4 H_{log rho}(X_p) / sum_P phi_P^2, taken along the abelian sigma_3 plane wave x_mu(x') = cos(kappa x'_nu) with nu != mu, has the series below for both kappa in {2pi/3, 4pi/3}. Through beta^10 it does not depend on kappa: for an axis momentum only (mu,nu) plaquettes carry flux, and no chair holds two of them, so sum_chairs phi^2 = 16 sum_P phi^2 in d = 4.
rows.predicted: d = 4: beta'_q = beta^4/64 - beta^6/384 + 125 beta^8/110592 - 389 beta^10/2211840 + O(beta^12). d = 3: beta^4/64 - beta^6/384 + 71 beta^8/110592 - 41 beta^10/552960 + O(beta^12). The same series at kappa = 2pi/3 and 4pi/3, and at kappa = pi/2, pi on coarse 4^4. Equivalently beta'_q = 2 c_half + 8 c_one + 16(d-2) c_chair, from the merged YM4-03C table.
rows.method: Route T (table): exact Hessians on the explicit rational plane wave (cos(2pi/3) = -1/2): chi_1/2(V_C) contributes phi_C^2/2, chi_1(V_P) contributes 2 phi_P^2, the chair phi_chair^2/2. These are weighted by the merged YM4-03C coefficients, in integers and Fractions. Route H (independent of the functional readout): rerun the merged YM4-03C Rust engine with every line link entered as exp(e x_l sigma_3), an exact polynomial jet in e through e^2. Read -d^2/de^2 of every polymer activity and every cluster term at e = 0, summed over classes with orbit factors, with G1 link degrees written as in YM4-03C. MET iff both routes give these rationals at both kappa.
rows.falsifier: Any coefficient through beta^10 differs from the prediction or between routes T and H, or the coefficients differ between kappa = 2pi/3 and 4pi/3 at any order <= 10.
rows.reachable: Route T: 81 coarse sites, integer arithmetic, seconds. Route H: the merged engine (25-40 s per receipt; 166,079 search states, 8 classes on fine 6^4) with a second-order jet per link, estimated under 10 minutes on 4 CPUs.

rows.statement: First momentum dependence of the strong-coupling coupling, oblique momenta. On coarse 4^4 (fine 8^4; the beta^10 coefficients are local for L >= 3), polarization mu, kappa(p) := sum_chairs phi_chair^2 / sum_P phi_P^2 - 16. Then beta'_q(p) - beta'_q(axis) = 2 c_chair kappa(p) beta^10 + O(beta^12), and there is no p dependence below beta^10.
rows.predicted: kappa(pi e_nu) = 0; kappa(pi(e_nu + e_lambda)) = -4; kappa(pi(e_nu + e_lambda + e_rho)) = -8 (nu, lambda, rho != mu). So beta'_q(pi(e_nu + e_lambda)) - beta'_q(axis) = -(3/65536) beta^10, and beta'_q(pi(e_nu + e_lambda + e_rho)) - beta'_q(axis) = -(3/32768) beta^10. Both differences are 0 at beta^4 through beta^8.
rows.method: Route T: enumerate the 48 chairs per coarse site as pairs of perpendicular coarse plaquettes sharing one link. Compute the abelian flux of each 6-link loop on the +-1 plane waves, in integers. Route H: the jet engine of CT01 run on fine 8^4 at the three momenta, reading the difference directly.
rows.falsifier: kappa differs from 0, -4 or -8, or route H reads a nonzero p dependence below beta^10 or a different beta^10 difference.
rows.reachable: Route T: 256 coarse sites and 12,288 chairs, integers, seconds. Route H: the same 8 classes on fine 8^4, minutes.

rows.statement: Scheme dependence at strong coupling through beta^10. Three exact gauge-invariant one-step couplings: beta'_S := 2 x (coefficient of chi_1/2(V_P) in log rho); beta'_chi, defined by <chi_1/2(V_P)>_nu = <chi_1/2(U_P)>_{Wilson beta', coarse 3^4}; and beta'_q from CT01. By Proposition 5, <chi_1/2(V_P)>_nu equals the fine 2x2 Wilson loop <chi_1/2(U_2x2)>_mu.
rows.predicted: beta'_S = beta^4/64 - beta^6/384 + beta^8/768 - 467 beta^10/1105920 + O(beta^12) (d = 4). beta'_chi - beta'_S = 0 through beta^10, in d = 4 and d = 3. beta'_q - beta'_S = -19 beta^8/110592 + 109 beta^10/442368 (d = 4) and -19 beta^8/110592 + 137 beta^10/884736 (d = 3). All three couplings agree through beta^6.
rows.method: beta'_chi by the moment route: the beta-series of <chi_1/2(U_2x2)>_mu from the engine's rho/integral(rho) series (gate G2), and independently from a route-S-style surface code with disk weights. That code counts the flat filling, 16 bumps, 16 domino disks, cubes on faces and off links, and the normalization clusters. Then invert against the coarse Wilson plaquette series 2 t_2(beta') + O(beta'^5), with t_2 from the exact Bessel series. Compare with beta'_S from the cumulant (log rho) series. All arithmetic in exact rationals.
rows.falsifier: beta'_chi differs from beta'_S at any order <= 10, or either difference to beta'_q is another rational.
rows.reachable: Merged engine plus a surface enumerator in a window of Z^4 (the YM4-03C derive checks used 352 to 672 cubes). Minutes.

rows.statement: First split between character matching and action projection, at beta^12. beta'_chi - beta'_S = 2 c_half^(4) c_one^(8) beta^12 + O(beta^14). Two cancellations make this the whole term: c_half's own beta^12 term cancels in the difference, and the -c_half^3/6 term from the Haar cumulant kappa_4(chi_1/2) = -1 cancels against the Wilson inversion 2 t_2(y) = y/2 - y^3/48. Products with chairs, N1, rectangles and disjoint pairs enter only at beta^14 or later, since their beta^8 coefficients read 0 in YM4-03C.
rows.predicted: beta'_chi - beta'_S = -19 beta^12/56623104 + O(beta^14), on fine 8^4 -> coarse 4^4 (d = 4) and on fine 8^3 (d = 3), the same value in both.
rows.method: Extend the YM4-03C engine to beta^12: triples of incompatible polymers, and coarse sides >= 4 so that the winding strip of P10a is absent. File both G2 series per class; take beta'_S from log rho and beta'_chi from rho/integral(rho), inverted as in CT03. Independent check: the surface route of CT03 extended to 12 plaquettes, with three-cluster normalization terms. A single-variable toy with exact Catalan moments reproduced the algebra at design time.
rows.falsifier: Any other beta^12 difference, or a nonzero difference at an order below 12.
rows.reachable: The search grows about tenfold per two plaquettes in YM4-03C (166,079 states at 10), so roughly 1.7 million states at 12, on fine 8^4 (24,576 plaquettes). Minutes to an hour per run; the three-polymer code is the effort. If it is not built, the row reads NOT_RUN, not MET.

rows.statement: The d = 2 coupling from the exact Theorem 8 flow, and the dimension dependence of the strong-coupling coupling. In d = 2, beta'_q(beta) = (1/3) sum n^2 (n^2 - 1) t_n^4 / sum n^2 t_n^4 with t_n = I_n(beta)/I_1(beta). This is computed independently of the 4D engine and must equal the d -> 2 value of CT01's formula (2 c_half + 8 c_one, planar coefficients).

The d = 2, 3, 4 coefficients are identical through beta^6. At beta^8 they are (17 + 54(d-2))/110592, slope +1/2048 per unit d; at beta^10 they are (122 - 450(d-2))/4423680, slope -5/49152 per unit d. The strong-coupling flow cannot tell d = 2 from d = 4 below beta^8.

rows.statement: The certified 4D window: the honest boundary of the available remainder theorem. On fine 6^4 (N_p = 7776): beta'_S(beta) lies in poly_10(beta) +- 2 M x^12/(1 - x^2), with x = beta N_p/r and M = -ln(2 - e^r) for r < ln 2. This rests on |log F_V(z)| <= M on |z| <= r/N_p (YM4-04A's argument), on the integral of |chi_1/2| over SU(2) being <= 1, and on P3 parity (even orders only). YM4-04A's disk is r = 1/4 with M = 1/2.

Best grid disk r = j/1024 with j <= 709 < 1024 ln2: certified with relative half-width <= 1/16 at 2^-22 (best j = 693, about 0.02425). At 2^-21, every grid disk that contains beta (j = 4..709) gives an interval containing 0 (smallest relative half-width about 6.207, at j = 693). Inside the certified window 0 < beta'_S < beta.

Rational upper and lower bounds on e^r (Taylor with remainder) and on -ln y (range reduction to [1/2, 1) plus series with tail bound). Upper bounds on M for the certification reads, lower bounds on M for the contains-0 reads.

rows.reachable: About 900 rational evaluations; 2.5 s at design time.

rows.statement: Asymptotic-freedom targets frozen as numbers, not as results. Along a renormalized trajectory at b = 2 for SU(2) with beta = 4/g^2: beta_{k+1} = beta_k - c0 - c1/beta_k + O(beta_k^-2), with c0 = 8 b0 ln2 = 11 ln2/(3 pi^2) and c1 = 32 b1 ln2 = 17 ln2/(3 pi^4). A single step from the Wilson action carries a scheme-dependent constant (compare CT09 and CT10 in d = 2), so c0 is a target only for the asymptotic step-to-step difference.
rows.method: pi from two Machin-type formulas (16 arctan(1/5) - 4 arctan(1/239), and 4(arctan(1/2) + arctan(1/3))) with alternating-series tail bounds. ln 2 from sum 1/(k 2^k) with a geometric tail, and independently from 2 artanh(1/3). Exact rational interval products.

rows.statement: The 2D positive control is certified at every coupling and the flow decreases. In d = 2, at b = 2 with the exact Theorem 8 map: beta'_q(beta) < beta for every beta > 0. Proof: the weights n^2 t_n^4 = (n^2 t_n) t_n^3, with t_n^3 strictly decreasing in n, so Chebyshev's sum inequality lowers the mean of n^2 - 1 below its m = 1 value 3 beta. The m = 1 identity (1/3) sum n^2(n^2-1) t_n / sum n^2 t_n = beta holds exactly.

Sums run to n_max with a certified geometric tail bound (n^2 t_n^4 <= n^2 exp(-2(n^2-1)/beta) bounds from the ratio). Independent route at beta <= 16: exact Bessel power series in rationals.

rows.statement: 2D weak-coupling asymptotics and scheme constants. Derived by Laplace's method and Euler-Maclaurin, using ln t_n = -(n^2-1)/(2 beta) - n^2/(4 beta^2) + n^4/(24 beta^3) + ..., uniform for n^2 of order beta: beta'_q(beta; m) = beta/m - 1/(2m) + 5/(6 m^2) - 1/3 + O(m/beta). Hence at m = 4, beta'_q = beta/4 - 13/32 + O(1/beta). From the fixed-n expansion, the character-matching coupling defined by t_2(beta'_chi) = t_2(beta)^4 is beta/4 + 3/8 + O(1/beta). The two gauge-invariant one-step couplings therefore differ by an O(1) constant at weak coupling, as a one-loop constant does in 4D. The limits are DERIVED; the 1/beta tolerances are the conjectured part.

rows.method: CT08's certified t_n enclosures; beta'_chi by certified bisection on t_2, which is increasing in beta (NAMED ratio monotonicity of I_{nu+1}/I_nu), to width 2^-40; exact rational comparisons.
rows.falsifier: Any of the seven inequalities fails on its certified enclosure.
rows.reachable: Seconds to a minute.

rows.statement: The 2D exact trajectory: a non-universal first step with a geometric approach to the fixed point. With beta_k := beta'_q(beta; m = 4^k) (k exact b = 2 steps), the one-step constant is s_k := beta_{k+1} - beta_k/4 = -1/4 - 5/(32 x 16^k) + O(4^k/beta). The limit -1/4 is the heat-kernel value, the 2D fixed-point action, and the deviation shrinks by 16 per step: the structure an H_k induction claims, in the one dimension where blocking closes. The limits are DERIVED; the tolerance is the conjectured part.
rows.predicted: At beta = 4096: s_0 in -13/32 +- 2^-14; s_1 in -133/512 +- 2^-14; s_2 in -2053/8192 +- 2^-14 (the design run read residuals below 3e-6). s_1 - s_0 and s_2 - s_1 are both positive.
rows.method: CT08's certified t_n enclosures at beta = 4096 and the sums with m = 1, 4, 16, 64; exact rational interval differences.
rows.falsifier: Any s_k leaves its interval, or the deviations from -1/4 fail to decrease.
rows.reachable: Seconds.

rows.statement: The heat-kernel control that fixes the meaning of -1/4. For K_q = sum n q^(n^2-1) chi_n with rational q = e^-tau, the Poisson (image) sum gives beta_q(q) = 1/(2 tau) - 1/3 + E(tau), with |E| of order e^(-pi^2/tau) times a polynomial. Hence beta_q(q^4) = (beta_q(q) + 1/3)/4 - 1/3 up to e^(-pi^2/(4 tau)) times a polynomial, exactly the s_infinity = -1/4 recursion.
rows.method: Exact rational partial sums of the character series at q and q^4 to n about 110, with certified geometric tails, and an exact rational comparison.
rows.falsifier: The certified difference is >= 10^-60.
rows.reachable: Rationals of about 60,000 bits; seconds.

rows.statement: Tree-level coupling of the iterated line map in d = 4: classical marginality, and an irrelevant part that grows like 2^k (thin lines; this turns the line-versus-average CONJECTURE of YM4-03 section 7 into exact numbers). r_k(p) := lim_{beta -> infinity} beta_k(p)/beta for B_{2^k}, transverse polarization mu, p = kappa e_nu. Alias formula: C'(p) = b^(2-d) sum over n_perp in Z_b^(d-1) of 1/khat^2((p + 2 pi n)/b) with n_mu = 0, and r = C'_W/C' with C'_W = 1/phat^2.
